The manifest declared no `quality_scale` key. It now declares **`platinum`**: every one of the 54 rules in `quality_scale.yaml` reads `done` or `exempt`, all four tiers are complete, and the cumulative derivation returns platinum. The declaration is derived from the register rather than transcribed into it, because a declared tier is a user-facing claim whose truth condition lives in a file that moves.

`--stats` and `checkPrBody` read the same `## Friction` section by two different rules, and the one the cron filer thresholds on was the wrong one. The template prescribes `none`, or one line per event: `<rule_id>: <unclear|contradiction|unenforced|stale|cost>: <evidence>`. `checkPrBody` has refused against that grammar since #614; `frictionIds` keyed a bullet on **the first backticked span of 2–80 characters on a list-marked line**, called any other marked line `(unlabelled friction bullet)`, and never read a line without a marker. Both readers now go through one exported function, `frictionEntries`, keyed on `<rule_id>`, and a list-marked line always opens an entry — so a bullet naming no rule and no class is refused by `pr-contract` instead of folding into the entry above as its evidence.

A graduation pass over the policy corpus: prose that a mechanical detector, or a rule the harness loads on the same path, already carries is cut or promoted to a pointer, so the corpus has room to grow again. It adds nothing except the two items reviews asked for today — the read-back evidence and the re-cut tie-break — plus one contract correction and one instrument fix, both below. **POLICY**: `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `tools/audit/briefs/`, `docs/HANDOVER.md`, both budget files. Leaves #201 open; closes nothing.

`pr-contract` read the pull-request body out of the event payload — `${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` — which is a snapshot taken when the event fired. `gh run rerun` replays that payload, so a body corrected after the event never reached the check. Measured on #1059 at head `a93a43b`: the body was edited to name `a93a43b`, run 35093322057 was re-run twice (attempts 2 and 3) and refused both times with the line quoted under `## Figures`, while `GET /pulls/1059` showed `## Head` naming `a93a43b`; the orchestrator unblocked it by close/reopen — a fresh event at the same head with no tree change — and run 35098726083 passed. The ledger lane edits its own PR's body with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, whose edits fire no `pull_request` event, so a manual re-run was the only route to green there and the one route that could not work.
